The Sacred Race of Wisdom and Devotion
In the celestial abode of Mount Kailash, a playful yet profound moment unfolded between the two divine brothers—
(also known as Kartikeya), the radiant sons of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati.
One day, the divine parents presented a challenge—simple in words, yet deep in meaning:
“Whoever travels around the world three times and returns first shall be declared the wisest and receive a special blessing.”

At once, Muruga—the youthful warrior, swift and brilliant—rose with confidence. Mounting his majestic peacock, his vehicle, he soared into the skies with blazing speed, determined to circle the vast earth.
Meanwhile, Ganesha, with his gentle eyes and thoughtful nature, remained still.
He did not compete with haste.
How vast is the world?” he pondered.
Then, with serene clarity, he rose, folded his hands, and began to walk in quiet reverence—circling not the earth, but his parents, Shiva and Parvati, three times.
With each step, he honored them as the very embodiment of the universe:
Parvati, the divine energy that creates and sustains all
To Ganesha, they were not just his parents…
, he bowed before them, calm and fulfilled.
Time passed, and Muruga returned—having circled oceans, mountains, forests, and skies. His journey was magnificent, his effort unquestionable. Yet, to his surprise, he found Ganesha already there.
When the truth was revealed, a gentle silence filled the space.
With loving smiles, Shiva and Parvati declared:
True wisdom is not in how far you travel, but in what you understand. To see the Divine in all—that is the greatest journey.”
Thus, Ganesha was blessed as the embodiment of wisdom, and the one invoked before all beginnings.
